budget_items.topic: Roland Acres water main replacement — cost review
budget_items.what_was_said: The board reviewed two cost figures for the in-house replacement job: the materials-only cost and a figure that adds the value of crew labor, comparing both to an estimate of what it would have cost to hire the job out at current 2023-era bids.
A commissioner proposed reinvesting the savings from doing the water main job in-house into a rubber-tire excavator and tandem-wheeler to allow the district to keep doing similar projects itself.

budget_items.topic: Possible new hire for in-house main work
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners discussed bringing on another employee in late winter/early spring to continue in-house main replacement work, and agreed to start putting together the annual expense estimate for staffing and equipment to present at a future meeting.
A commissioner said pursuing the zero-percent-interest SRF loan option was estimated to save a large sum compared to conventional financing.

budget_items.topic: O&M cost differential between water source options (survey)
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident presented his own analysis arguing the operations-and-maintenance cost difference between two water-source combination options was understated in the district's consultant figures, using a baseline and a variable-cost percentage split; the district said its consultants (Tighe & Bond) were confident in their numbers but did not have them itemized as a line item.

budget_items.topic: Capital cost of the three-well treatment option
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident questioned why moving from a two-source to a three-source treatment configuration added several million dollars in capital cost; the superintendent explained it required a larger treatment plant and a raw water transmission main.

decisions.decision: Staff will begin putting together annual expense projections for hiring an additional employee and for equipment, to bring to a future meeting as part of a three-to-five-year plan.
The community engagement survey draft will be finalized and brought back to the board for approval before release, alongside a draft postcard mailer and website.

The district will continue pursuing removal of the Woodlands condo trust's kayak racks from the Zone One well protection area, through its attorney if necessary, and will seek to recover costs from the Woodlands if legal action becomes necessary.

The clerk/president will look into whether the district's bylaws allow shutting off a ratepayer for non-compliance with district regulations (not just non-payment), and report back at the next meeting.
The board will ask town counsel whether an alternative voting method (e.g., a paper ballot period before the meeting) could legally be offered to increase ratepayer participation.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners reviewed the in-house cost of the Roland Acres water main replacement versus hiring it out, discussed a near-final draft of a community engagement survey on water source options, and spent significant time on the Woodlands condo trust's refusal to remove kayak racks from the well's Zone One protection area, concluding they will pursue legal action if the racks are not voluntarily moved. The meeting also covered SRF grant funding status, a possible new hire and equipment purchase for future in-house projects, a proposal to explore alternative voting methods for ratepayers, and recognized the superintendent's 40th work anniversary, closing with extended public comment challenging the survey's cost estimates.

what_happened.line: Commissioners will pursue legal action against the Woodlands condo trust if it does not voluntarily remove kayak racks from the well's Zone One protection area.
The board compared the in-house cost of the Roland Acres water main replacement, including crew labor, against an estimate of hiring the work out.
A near-final community survey on water source options will be finalized and brought back for board approval before release.
Staff will begin multi-year expense projections for a possible new hire and equipment purchase to continue in-house main work.
A resident disputed the district's operations-and-maintenance cost comparison between water source options; the district said the consultant's figures were not broken out as a line item.

why_it_matters: Zone One is the well's legal protection area, so this dispute touches the long-term security of the town's water supply, not just a neighborhood nuisance.
The community survey will shape which water source option the district pursues, and residents will likely be asked to weigh in on it once finalized.
The in-house-versus-contracted cost comparison, and any new hire or equipment purchase, feed directly into future water rates and capital spending.
watch_next: The finalized survey draft, once brought back to the board for approval, plus its postcard mailer and website.
The clerk/president's report on bylaw authority to shut off non-compliant ratepayers, and town counsel's opinion on alternative voting methods, due at the next meeting.
